purpose: Public-safe evidence references for the judge/developer start page; no prediction of eligibility or prize outcome.

publicPayments.claim: Two distinct developer-funded testnet payment rights were collected by the same beneficiary.

historicalOutage.scope: Operator-controlled public A routes returned HTTP 503 before second funding and again after second claim; B routes returned HTTP 200 in those probes. A was then restored.

limits: Chain receipts establish the approved payment outcomes, not which device, passkey or UI was used.
The builder reported completion after existing-key B instructions; physical authentication was not independently observed.
This is developer-funded testnet demonstration activity, not revenue, demand or external adoption.

separateAppRecovery.existingPasskeyReuse: The instructions explicitly required the same existing key; completion was reported. Credential identity was not independently correlated.
separateAppRecovery.httpCorroboration: Published app routes, successful preparation and later reserve reads were recorded; redacted metadata does not prove decryption or exported bytes.

separateCrossDeviceReport.scope: Earlier single-text text-v1 test following Mac Safari preparation to iPhone Safari recovery instructions.

hostingLimits: The published editors share one recovery origin and its trust boundary.
Hosted text collection uses its single-store configuration; separate local replica processes are a different evidence scope.
No independent second operator, provider, machine or public domain migration is established.
Closing A is not an HTTP outage; no public outage is established for the two-editor iPhone sequence.

localTamperAndFailureTests.scope: Installed public SDK, synthetic credential, two app namespaces and separate real loopback SQLite storage processes.
localTamperAndFailureTests.primaryBoundary: Original-app requests were forbidden; this particular proof did not start A and does not establish a deployed A outage.

meraUse.nonAccountPurpose: Discoverable user-verified PRF material locates and decrypts immutable app text; text recovery creates no account or signing session.
meraUse.derivation: One protocol-wide PRF salt; HKDF binds the app ID, exact recovery origin, RP and selected credential, with separate locator, manifest-encryption and text-encryption purposes. The PRF salt is not app-specific.
meraUse.crossDeviceDependency: The same existing credential must be available on a compatible authenticator at the original recovery RP. This is not lost-passkey recovery or arbitrary domain migration.
limits: Editors receive plaintext and intentional exports are plaintext.
App namespace separation does not protect against a malicious client on the shared recovery origin.
A retained encrypted export is a viable alternative; general superiority to backup is not established.

preciseGaps.detail: Physical execution of the newer one-assertion multi-app or replicated flow is not established. Keep that feature under local automated evidence unless a new demonstration is deliberately performed.
Existing iPhone and earlier Mac-to-iPhone reports need no generic repeat. They do not supply an independently observed live cross-device comparison or inspected export bytes for the newer flow.
Project-authored editor integrations and internal reviews are not third-party integration, user retention or adoption.
Separate local stores and an operator-controlled A outage do not prove independent operators or providers.
Video and final submission are outside this verification; this map claims neither completion nor sponsor acceptance.

maintenanceHostedRelease.detail: Both existing public Try sites publish version 9. All 54 static/config checks passed; 36 responses are raw byte-exact and 18 HTML responses preserve application HTML with a recorded hosting insertion. Existing frontend profiles match approved bindings. No new native recovery or export was performed.
